rulings.evidence: Not a form flip: sriracha IS a sauce, so 'Sriracha sauce' is a rename onto the existing vocabulary row Sriracha [sriracha], with no change of product, price class or gram weight. Declined the board's generic hot-sauce match, which prices Louisiana-style bottles rather than this chili-garlic paste.

Reuse of the live limes id (5 of 7, cheapest 0.25 at Walmart), following the 2026-08-27 'fresh lime juice' and 'Lime Wedges' rulings that price whole limes squeezed. Named 'limes' to match the food-DB row this batch already carries.

Refused the board's generic lettuce id: romaine is variety priced (romaine hearts are a separate SKU well above a head of iceberg), which is the standing red-onion-is-not-onions and cherry-tomatoes-are-not-tomatoes rejection. New id proposed to the registrar; 'shredded' is a cut, not a form flip.

rulings.raw: 8 Corn or flour tortillas (store-bought or homemade, warmed)
rulings.evidence: The source offers a choice and corn is listed first, so the line resolves to the same-form vocabulary row Corn Tortillas [corn-tortillas]; the board carries tortillas at 7 of 7. Corn and flour are different foods at different gram weights, so only one may be priced and weighed.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Romaine is not already priced under another spelling: the pre-resolve board matcher returned only the generic `lettuce` id for this term and no vocabulary row shares a core word with it, and no romaine, cos or 'romaine hearts' spelling surfaced in any near-row list for this batch. It is a genuinely different commodity from `lettuce` (iceberg/head basis) on both price and pack - romaine sells as 3-count hearts or a whole head at a clearly higher shelf price - which is the same variety-pricing distinction the estate already enforces for red onion vs onions and cherry tomatoes vs tomatoes. If a romaine id already exists under another name this is a reuse, not a new mint, and the line should take that id.
